text: Build an approval process, submit one quote, watch it land in the right queue, and it's tempting to call it done. One successful run proves the happy path works. It proves almost nothing else.

Four categories, every time: the happy path it was built for, boundary values sitting exactly at the edge of a condition, bulk changes to many records at once, and negative cases the automation should never touch at all.

Applied to Harborline's quote approval: fifteen percent routes correctly. Exactly ten percent should NOT enter approval. Fifty quotes updated at once through a data import. A quote with the discount field left blank entirely.

Every one of those tests belongs in a sandbox or Developer Edition org, never production. Debug logs confirm exactly which criteria evaluated true or false for a given record -- not just that nothing visibly broke.
A quote entering approval when it shouldn't is a failure, even if zero errors appear anywhere on screen. The process 'running' and the process running on the right record are two different things.
Two case studies, a documentation method, a practice lab, and now testing. Next lesson brings all of Chapter 3 together in a review.
